import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Layout

```
backend/
├── package.json        workspaces, turbo, the root db:* and dc:* shortcuts
├── turbo.json          build → typecheck, lint, test, dev all depend on ^build
├── compose.yml         Postgres + Redis (+ Temporal) for every app
├── compose.test.yml    the API's test stack
├── .forgejo/           root CI: one pipeline for every workspace
├── apps/
│   ├── api/            nest-api, minus its prisma/ folder
│   └── worker/         node-worker, minus its prisma/ folder
└── packages/
    └── db/             prisma/schema, prisma/migrations, the compiled client
```

Inside `apps/api` and `apps/worker`, everything is as in
[nest-api](../../nest-api/architecture/) and
[node-worker](../../node-worker/architecture/).

## The shared Prisma package

`packages/db` is the only place a Prisma client is generated. Its `build`
script runs `prisma generate` and then compiles the generated TypeScript to
`dist/` as **CommonJS**, and its `exports` map serves `dist/*`:

```ts
import { Prisma, PrismaClient } from '@scope/db/client';
import { Gender } from '@scope/db/enums';
```

CommonJS because the two apps disagree on module format: the Nest API is
CommonJS, the worker is ESM, and ESM can import CommonJS but not the other way
round without extra loader flags. One build serves both.

Both apps depend on it as `"@scope/db": "workspace:*"`, so
`node_modules/@scope/db` is a symlink to `packages/db`. Turbo's `^build` makes
every app task wait for it: `build`, `typecheck`, `test` and `dev` never see a
stale or missing client.

<Aside title="The apps run the compiled client">
After a schema change outside turbo, `yarn db:generate` rebuilds `dist/`. A
running `yarn dev` keeps the old client loaded until it restarts: Nest's watch
and `tsx watch` don't watch `node_modules`.
</Aside>

## Who owns what

- **The API owns the database.** Its `db:*` scripts load the API's own `.env`
  (or `.env.test`, `.env.production`) and run Prisma inside `@scope/db`. The
  seeders stay in the API, because they create users through better-auth.
- **The worker never migrates.** It imports the client and gets every model
  the API has.
- **Compose is shared.** The API's `dc:*` scripts drive the root
  `compose.yml`; the worker points at the same Postgres and Redis.

## Dependencies

One `yarn.lock` at the root. A dependency goes in the workspace that imports
it; the root holds only `turbo` and Prettier.

The API installs into its own `apps/api/node_modules`
(`installConfig.hoistingLimits: "workspaces"`). Its test library, Suites,
finds its Vitest adapter by resolving it from beside `@suites/unit`, and with
the two hoisted to different places every spec that builds a `TestBed` fails.
The cost: root binaries such as `turbo` aren't on the PATH inside `apps/api`,
so turbo commands run from the root.
